items.name: KFC
clues: Embarrassing, and for about a week the whole country was talking about it.
Hungry customers all over the UK. Some even complained to the police.
In February 2018 a new delivery company took over the deliveries, and hundreds of restaurants ran out of their one main ingredient.
The company apologised with a full-page newspaper advert that made people laugh, and the advert won awards.
On the advert, the letters on the famous red-and-white bucket were rearranged into a rude word.
The Colonel's restaurants ran out of chicken.

items.name: Pepsi
clues: A big, glossy advert that was meant to bring people together. It didn't.
People who had marched in real protests, and pretty much everyone on Twitter.
In 2017 the advert seemed to suggest that a fizzy drink could solve a tense stand-off between protesters and the police.
The company pulled the advert about a day after it came out and said it had “missed the mark”.
A reality-TV star and model walks out of a photo shoot, joins a march and hands a police officer a can.
The drink in the can was Coca-Cola's biggest rival.

items.name: The Oscars
clues: Live on television, in front of millions of people, and nobody on stage knew what to do.
The people who had just been told they'd won, and then told they hadn't.
In February 2017 two famous actors were handed the wrong envelope and read out the wrong winner.
Somebody came on stage during the winners' speeches and said there had been a mistake. The accountancy firm in charge of the envelopes apologised.
“La La Land” was announced as the best film of the year, but the real winner was “Moonlight”.
It's Hollywood's biggest night, and the prize is a small golden statue.

items.name: Boaty McBoatface
clues: It started as a friendly idea and ended with an organisation looking slightly silly in front of the whole country.
Scientists who had hoped for a serious name, and the government minister who had to sort it out.
In 2016 a UK research council let the public suggest and vote on a name for its new £200 million polar research ship.
The ship got a famous naturalist's name in the end, and the winning name went on a small yellow robot submarine instead.
A radio presenter suggested the winning name as a joke, and it got more than 124,000 votes.
Its name is the word “boat” turned into a Scottish-sounding surname and first name.

items.name: Galaxy Note 7
clues: A brand-new product that was supposed to be the company's best ever, and lasted only a few weeks.
Airlines, and anybody who had just bought one.
Soon after its launch in August 2016, some of its batteries overheated and caught fire.
The company recalled every one it had sold, even the replacements, and stopped making it in October 2016.
For a while, before every flight, passengers were told it was not allowed on board.
A big-screen smartphone from South Korea's biggest company.

items.name: Cyberpunk 2077
clues: Years of excitement, and then a huge disappointment on the first day.
Gamers, especially people who played on older consoles.
When it finally came out in December 2020, it was so full of bugs that it was almost unplayable on some machines.
Sony removed it from its online store and offered refunds. It only went back on sale there in June 2021, and many fans now say it's great.
Keanu Reeves is in it.
A video game from Poland, set in Night City in the future.
